newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA inmates blast fellow Basque rebels for killing.
newsitem.headline: ETA inmates blast fellow Basque rebels for killing.

text.p: Three jailed ETA guerrillas publicly condemned their Basque rebel comrades on Friday for killing a young Spanish politician, adding their voices to a national outcry against the radical separatists.

The three men read a statement at a Basque prison saying that with the killing of 29-year-old Miguel Angel Blanco, ETA had in recent days "managed to accumulate more hate than in 38 years of terrorism."

Jose Manuel Soares Gamboa, Luis Gaston and Luis Gorriti, repentant members of the separatist group that was formed in 1959, also denounced ETA's political wing Herri Batasuna, saying every vote for the radical party was another bullet for ETA.

"After today, ETA has thousands of bullets fewer and this is good, it's the best thing that could happen to us," Soares Gamboa said, reading a statement to reporters at the Nanclares de Oca prison near the Basque capital Vitoria.
"I condemn ETA, I condemn Herri Batasuna, I condemn your crimes and your tortures."

Soares Gamboa, who was sentenced to more than 100 years in prison for involvement in a series of killings, turned himself in to Spanish authorities in 1994 and has since expressed regret in interviews and court appearances.
He said Herri Batasuna lawyers told him in court that it would cost him dearly for speaking out against ETA.
Gaston is in prison awaiting trial on charges of belonging to an armed band, and Gorriti has served three years of a 38-year sentence for various crimes.

The prisoners' public pronouncement was another sign of the divisions emerging among radical Basque separatists after Blanco's killing last weekend. The assassination shocked Spaniards, bringing millions to the streets in angry protests.
Several others among the 500-odd ETA prisoners as well as growing numbers of Herri Batasuna members have shown signs of their disillusionment with the armed struggle after the latest attack.

One ETA inmate went on a hunger strike in protest and others observed a 10-minute silent tribute to the victim. A Herri Batasuna deputy in the Navarre region pleaded with ETA to spare Blanco's life and later condemned his killing.
Herri Batasuna had planned to counter the criticism on Saturday with a demonstration in the Basque city of San Sebastian.
But the Basque government on Thursday barred the group from going ahead with the rally for fear it would provoke a violent backlash at a time when anti-ETA emotions were running high.
Herri Batasuna filed an appeal, and a Basque court on Friday upheld the government ban. The group said earlier it would abide by the court's ruling.
There have been scattered attacks on Herri Batasuna supporters and offices since the killing, raising fears of a more widespread civilian conflict in the region.

Basques have long kept quiet out of fear of retaliation from the radical group, which has killed some 800 people in its struggle for an independent Basque state. But the massive nationwide protests awakened a new spirit of defiance.
Politicians who once would never have dared speak ill of ETA started proceedings on Friday to oust the Herri Batasuna mayor of Mondragon, a stronghold of diehard Basque nationalism.

This was the first tangible move toward isolating the radical politicians. Basque political leaders and the central government in Madrid have vowed to minimise contact with Herri Batasuna politicians, who are seen as apologists for violence.

Police found an ETA hideout packed with weapons in the Basque town of Durango on Thursday. On Friday, police arrested a woman who lived in the apartment, which was found when some bomb-making materials exploded, state radio reported.

Blanco was kidnapped last Thursday by rebels demanding the transfer of 500 ETA inmates to prisons in the autonomous Basque region within 48 hours. The government refused and ETA shot him twice in the head on Saturday. He died 12 hours later.

ETA attacks have triggered public anger in the past, but it was the death sentence carried out against such an ordinary person that cut to the heart of Spanish society and sparked an unprecedented outcry.
